customConcept.name: Starbucks (company-operated)
customConcept.blurb: A drive-thru Starbucks where three cars in four never come inside, the mobile orders never stop, and a latte is the whole business.

state.circumstances: You're the store manager of a company-operated Starbucks with a drive-thru on a busy road outside Phoenix. Starbucks owns the store, the menu, the equipment and the rota software; you run the partners, the drive-thru times and the mobile-order wall, and you're paid a salary and a bonus on the store's results.

features.name: Drive-thru lane with a digital menu board
features.pitch: A single lane round the building with a pickup window; most of the store's orders go through it.

features.name: Mobile Order & Pay handoff plane
features.pitch: A pickup counter for app orders placed ahead, with the Starbucks Rewards app driving repeat visits.

setting.name: Arterial road, Phoenix suburbs
setting.desc: A freestanding drive-thru Starbucks on a six-lane arterial between a grocery-anchored plaza and a freeway on-ramp. Commuters from 5:30am, school-run parents, remote workers with laptops by ten, a heat-driven cold-drink rush every summer afternoon.

ev.text: Afternoons over 110°F. Hot-drink sales stop dead and the cold-bar can't keep up.
A Dutch Bros opened a double drive-thru half a mile down the road.

desk.title: The drive-thru is backing onto the road
desk.text: At 7:30am the queue blocks a lane of the arterial and the city has noticed.

choices.label: Put a partner outside with a tablet to take orders down the line
Leave it; the queue is a sign of success

mods.label: Starbucks support center, technology and licensing

world.notes: Starbucks FY2024 10-K: North America company-operated stores took $24.26 billion across about 10,900 stores on average (roughly $2.2 million a store). Company-operated sales are 74% beverages, 23% food, 3% other. Product and distribution costs were 27.7% of North America revenue and store operating expenses 51.4% of company-operated store revenue; North America operating margin was 19.8%. In FY2024 US comparable transactions fell 5% while average ticket rose 4%. Starbucks is expanding drive-thru formats. Grande prices (typical, 2025): brewed coffee $2.95, latte about $5.05, cold brew $4.45, chai latte $5.35, caramel macchiato $5.45, Frappuccinos about $6. The store's name and number, its staff, rent, district manager and local events are invented; menu food prices and the manager's pay are estimates.

supplierPool.name: Starbucks distribution center
supplierPool.blurb: Starbucks' own supply chain: coffee from its roasting plants, food, syrups, cups and lids on scheduled trucks from the regional distribution center. Store managers don't choose suppliers.

supplierPool.name: Regional dairy on Starbucks' contract
supplierPool.blurb: Milk and plant-based milks delivered several times a week by the dairy Starbucks contracts for the region.

team.name: Denise Carrillo
team.bio: Assistant store manager. Came up as a barista at this store, writes the deployment chart for every peak and can hear a drive-thru timer from the back room.

team.name: Marcus Tran
team.bio: Shift supervisor who runs the bar at the morning peak and trains every new partner on milk steaming. Full-time, on the hourly scale.

profile.name: Starbucks Corporation
profile.kind: publicly traded coffee company based in Seattle
profile.desc: About 40,200 stores worldwide at the end of fiscal 2024, 18,400 of them in North America, 11,161 run by the company itself. Company-operated stores are about 74% beverages.
profile.personality: Run on standards, dashboards and a turnaround plan. Under Brian Niccol, CEO since September 2024, the 'Back to Starbucks' programme wants the café to feel like a coffeehouse again: faster handoffs, for-here mugs, handwritten names on cups, fewer menu items.

rep.name: Alicia Moreno
rep.title: District manager
rep.style: Covers a dozen stores, visits yours every couple of weeks, checks drive-thru times and the Customer Connection score before she says hello, and wants to know who you're developing into a shift supervisor.

events.text: The Pumpkin Spice Latte came back for the autumn and the drive-thru line wrapped the building for a week.
The holiday red cups arrived, and with them the busiest weeks of the year.

desk.title: A union election at your store
desk.text: A group of partners has filed with the labour board to join Starbucks Workers United, as hundreds of Starbucks stores have. Alicia reminds you what managers may and may not say.

choices.label: Stay strictly neutral and keep the store running
choices.blurb: The vote goes ahead; morale holds.

choices.label: Hold a 'listening session' about the company's benefits
choices.blurb: Some partners call it an anti-union meeting.

effects.hook: the outcome of the union vote at the Starbucks store

events.text: Corporate cut a batch of slow-selling drinks from the menu nationwide. Two regulars complained that their order no longer exists.

desk.title: The district wants faster handoffs
desk.text: The new target is four minutes from order to handoff, and your store runs closer to six at the morning peak.

choices.label: Add a partner to the bar at peak

policies.name: Health insurance for partners on 20+ hours
policies.blurb: Starbucks offers medical, dental and vision to partners averaging 20 hours a week; the company pays most of the premium.

policies.name: Starbucks College Achievement Plan
policies.blurb: Full tuition for a first bachelor's degree through Arizona State University's online programme, for partners working enough hours.
